citation: [1912 S. Prairie Ave. (Moulton / Lowden residence).] Photograph of the house's street front from the walk, close to, looking up past its stoop; unknown photographer, undated (an electric street lamp stands at the right). Reproduced on chicagology.com, Prairie Avenue, 1912 S. Prairie.
author: unknown photographer
describes_date: undated; the electric lamp places it after the district's 1904 gas lamps
repository: chicagology.com (secondary reproduction; the original holder is not named). Prairie library image a19-cgy-1912-exterior, recorded there as 'unknown - link only'; the project's reference copy is the image store's (kevinrhaas/chicago-images, prairie-1904/files/a19-cgy-1912-exterior.jpg).
locator: The whole print: the street front from its north gable past the round bay to the entrance under its striped awning, the stoop with its cheek walls, the iron railing on the coping, and the electric lamp at the curb.
rights_note: A secondary web reproduction whose original source and rights are not stated (the Prairie library's own ruling: 'unknown - link only'). Only forms and places are read from it; nothing is derived from the image as an asset.
access_notes: Read 2026-10-27 (T-3203) from the image store's reference copy, 1218 x 1974 px greyscale, sha256 edfbb93fb891e8f549e6aa782b2609f7a7b6fcde87847a46fbce72e00c350010.
note: Ivy covers the north part of the front and the round bay up to the third storey's sills, and runs along the belt course over the entrance block; the stoop, its cheek walls and the railing on the coping are clear of it. Ivy of that reach is years old, so T-3203 plants it on the 1904 house as inferred rather than attested.
what_it_supplies: the ivy over 1912's street front and round bay, and how far up it reaches
what_it_does_not_supply: the front yard before the coping, which the print crops
